name: EIWZ Extreme Title
epitaph: Pain won the belt in a ten-man Royal Rumble main event at Christmas Bash 1998 and retained it against Jazz five days later — the only two documented moments in this title's own surviving lineage. CWF-Pro's own already-served Ultra Extreme Hardcore Title ledger later records the belt unified into its own, defeating Pain in the process, years after the events held here.

name: EIWZ North American Title
epitaph: Flint won the belt via disqualification over Jazz at Christmas Bash 1998 and lost it to Triple X five days later — the only two documented moments in this title's own surviving lineage. CWF-Pro's own already-served Intercontinental Title ledger later records the belt unified into its own, defeating Flint in the process, years after the events held here.

name: EIWZ European Title
epitaph: Havok won a tournament final over Pain to claim the belt at Christmas Bash 1998 and retained it against Annihilator five days later — the only two documented moments in this title's own surviving lineage. CWF-Pro's own already-served Canadian Title ledger later records the belt unified into its own, defeating Havok in the process, years after the events held here.

name: EIWZ Light Weight Title
epitaph: Necromancer won an eleven-man Royal Rumble to claim the belt at Christmas Bash 1998 and retained it against The Creep five days later — the only two documented moments in this title's own surviving lineage. CWF-Pro's own already-served Royal Title ledger later records the belt unified into its own, defeating Necromancer in the process, years after the events held here.

name: EIWZ Tag Team Title
epitaph: Cool Moe "D" and SCSU Pimpster won the belts in a Royal Rumble-style tag match at Christmas Bash 1998, the only documented moment in this title's own surviving lineage. CWF-Pro's own already-served World Tag Team Titles ledger later records the belts unified into its own, defeating the pair in the process, years after the event held here.
